title: Cucumber and cabbage bulgur bowls with tahini

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a simple staple; tahini is just ground sesame and is on the cupboard list.

supermarket.reason: Bulgur, tahini, pumpkin seeds and the fresh vegetables are all everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a kettle, a bowl and a small frying pan, with nothing beyond chopping and soaking.

works.reason: 200g bulgur to 400ml water is a sound ratio, and with a tin of chickpeas, half a cabbage and a cucumber it makes a fair lunch for four with a well-seasoned dressing.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers shredding, chopping, toasting and whisking while the bulgur soaks for its 15 unattended minutes, which suits a quick lunch.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the mint and lemon, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A crunchy raw cucumber and radish bowl suits early May, and the cucumber is a main part of the salad rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Wholegrain bulgur, chickpeas, yoghurt, seeds and plenty of vegetables make a filling, balanced lunch.
